summary: Establishes the four-post digital product core across the three-year mobilisation, with lean shared institutional support, to deliver King’s Edge and the Digital Student Experience Hub and build an enduring product-development capability.
detailSummary:
Digital Innovation and Product Development Capability establishes the team and working practices through which King’s Edge and the Digital Student Experience Hub are delivered. The current planning assumption is that the same four-post core is required throughout the three-year mobilisation to June 2029, rather than being a Year One-only team. Evidence still determines whether additional capacity is needed and which elements should continue beyond mobilisation.

The funded core is 4.0 FTE across four explicit posts, each with its own year-by-year planning profile. The Senior Backend & Integration Engineer (1.0 FTE) owns backend services, domain/API integration, technical integration with King’s systems and senior engineering judgement; the planning assumption is King’s Grade 8 midpoint, approximately £61,000 for the eight-month November 2026 to June 2027 mobilisation period and £91,000 in each full year thereafter. The Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer (1.0 FTE) provides hands-on delivery across the student-facing Hub, King’s Edge and supporting application services; the Grade 7 midpoint planning profile is approximately £50,000 in Year One and £75,000 in each full year. The Product & Service Designer (1.0 FTE) combines UX and interaction design, UI design, service and journey design, prototyping, student/user research and usability testing; the Grade 7 midpoint profile is likewise approximately £50,000 then £75,000 per full year. The QA Engineer (1.0 FTE) owns product test strategy, automated and manual quality assurance, regression and release quality; the Grade 6 midpoint profile is approximately £42,000 in Year One and £63,000 in each full year. The QA Year One estimate assumes the full eight-month planning period for a conservative baseline, although a later start once code production is established would reduce actual spend. These estimates include employer pension, employer National Insurance and apprenticeship levy. Together they profile at approximately £203,000 in 2026/27, £304,000 in 2027/28 and £304,000 in 2028/29, or approximately £811,000 across the mobilisation in constant 2026 planning prices. Digital and IT / HR must validate final grades, appointment points, start dates and future pay awards.

Mark Peace is the Product Owner during mobilisation, so no additional Product Owner post or fractional allocation is required in the resource model. The four funded posts are supported by a deliberately small amount of shared institutional capacity: approximately 0.2 FTE Business Analyst during the main discovery period to map systems, information flows, ownership, dependencies and operational readiness; approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support from Digital and IT for Azure, environments, deployment pipelines and observability; and up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer cannot credibly carry that function. Specialist security, privacy, accessibility, data, architecture assurance and service-management input is drawn from existing institutional functions when required rather than represented as standing fractional posts. Product quality assurance remains the responsibility of the QA Engineer.

The substantive build demand begins with King’s Edge, with the same team establishing and then evolving the reusable Hub foundations and wider student-facing product under 4.1.2. The Year One baseline includes a £90,000 planning allowance for ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling so the experienced engineering team can test and use agentic development as a material productivity accelerator. The amount is based on the 28 August Digital and IT discussion and remains subject to commercial validation, including whether existing shared capacity can reduce the eventual cost. No Year Two or Year Three agentic-tooling cost is assumed yet; later tooling investment should follow Year One commercial and productivity evidence. The existing KAI team is not assumed to transfer wholesale into the capability, but reusable technical assets, including Azure AI Foundry components, should be assessed and adopted where they fit the target architecture.

The current Year One cash baseline across 4.1.2 and 4.1.3 remains approximately £358,000: £203,000 across the four individually costed product-team posts, £50,000 Azure/environments/platform, £15,000 paid student co-design and £90,000 agentic software-development tooling. The core staffing profile is now also explicit for Years Two and Three at approximately £304,000 per full year. Other Year Two and Year Three investment should be added only where the product roadmap and live evidence justify it. By the end of the three-year mobilisation, King’s should have both delivered substantial product capability and enough evidence to decide the recurrent business-as-usual team, tooling and funding model.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s does not currently have a sufficiently dependable multidisciplinary product capability for turning emerging student-experience needs into working, supported digital services at pace. Requirements can be addressed through conventional system change, local initiatives, temporary projects or standalone products, making prioritisation and reuse difficult.

King’s needs sustained in-house capability to deliver the King’s Edge roadmap, establish and evolve the Digital Student Experience Hub, and support broader discovery and integration across the student digital estate. Treating the four-post core as a Year One-only team would understate the delivery capacity required for the remainder of the three-year mobilisation.
caseForChange.opportunity:
An explicit four-post funded product core across the three-year mobilisation, combined with a lean shared Business Analysis, DevOps/platform and conditional solution-architecture model, gives King’s a disciplined route from need to supported change without overcomplicating the team. Combining UX/UI, service design and user research in the Product & Service Designer keeps discovery close to product delivery, while dedicated QA protects release quality. Ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling gives the experienced engineering team a practical Year One test of whether agentic development can materially increase throughput without weakening engineering judgement or quality.

King’s Edge supplies the first substantive product demand. The Digital Student Experience Hub extends that work into reusable shared foundations and progressively deeper institutional journeys across the remainder of the mobilisation.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge is moving into rapid replatforming and substantial product development, while the Digital Student Experience Hub needs a focused September 2027 first release and then sustained development across the remainder of the mobilisation.

2026/27 is therefore the right point to recruit the four funded posts and secure the small shared capacities they depend on, but the financial model also needs to recognise that these posts remain necessary in Years Two and Three. Future expansion beyond this core should follow evidence about throughput, journey demand, integration complexity, quality and operational load.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
King’s has a dependable multidisciplinary digital product capability with a transparent pipeline, clear decision rights and repeatable practices for discovery, design, engineering, quality, assurance, release and continuous improvement.

Across the three-year mobilisation, the funded 4.0 FTE core delivers the King’s Edge roadmap and the Digital Student Experience Hub. Each funded post is costed separately by academic year, including the pro-rata mobilisation period in Year One and full-year staffing in Years Two and Three. Mark Peace acts as Product Owner. The Product & Service Designer combines UX/UI, service design and user research. Shared institutional support is kept deliberately lean: approximately 0.2 FTE Business Analysis during the main discovery period, approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, and up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if the senior engineering role cannot absorb it, with specialist assurance drawn on demand. A £90,000 planning allowance provides ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling for the Year One engineering model.

The capability can expand beyond the four-post core where live demand and evidence justify it. By June 2029, King’s should have enough evidence to decide which elements of the mobilisation team and tooling should continue as recurrent business-as-usual capability rather than carrying the four posts forward automatically.

benefits.title: King’s responds more quickly to emerging student needs
benefits.statement: Priority needs can be translated into tested digital responses in shorter cycles, with student and staff evidence shaping development before large commitments are made.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From establishment of the first delivery pipeline
benefits.successLooksLike: Priority needs move predictably from discovery to evaluated live use, and users can influence solutions while they remain adaptable.

benefits.title: Digital delivery becomes more predictable and evidence-led
benefits.statement: A transparent pipeline, explicit capacity decisions and consistent product and assurance practices make needs, priorities, progress and trade-offs clearer.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.realisationPeriod: As the operating model becomes routine
benefits.successLooksLike: Demand is prioritised through one route, delivery commitments are visible and changes in team capacity can be explained by actual roadmap evidence.

benefits.title: Successful innovation becomes sustainable institutional provision
benefits.statement: Valuable changes have a defined route into secure, supported and appropriately owned operation, while multidisciplinary capability remains available for continuous improvement.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.successLooksLike: Successful capabilities have explicit ownership and support arrangements, unsuccessful trials close cleanly, and the product capability has an evidence-based route into business as usual.

steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the core multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: From September through November 2026, secure three-year mobilisation funding and recruit or assign four core posts through Digital and IT: 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, 1.0 FTE Product & Service Designer and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer. The Year One November-to-June cost profile is approximately £61,000, £50,000, £50,000 and £42,000 respectively; full-year planning costs are approximately £91,000, £75,000, £75,000 and £63,000 in each of Years Two and Three. Confirm final grading and appointment points with Digital and IT / HR. Confirm Mark Peace as Product Owner, approximately 0.2 FTE protected Business Analysis, approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, and up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if not covered by the senior engineering post. Confirm the commercial route for the £90,000 Year One ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling allowance.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish one transparent pipeline, prioritisation and capacity cadence, proportionate discovery and user involvement, engineering and quality expectations, agentic-development practices, embedded assurance and release practices across King’s Edge and the Digital Student Experience Hub.

steps.title: Prove the capability through King’s Edge, broad discovery and the focused Hub release
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, prove that the four-post funded core and lean shared-capacity model can deliver the substantive King’s Edge roadmap and focused Digital Student Experience Hub release while the Product & Service Designer leads integrated experience discovery and design. Measure the contribution of agentic development alongside quality and rework, and use evidence to identify any capacity gap beyond the funded core.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make operating practices routine across the live Digital Student Experience Hub and King’s Edge product domain, balancing roadmap delivery, incidents, maintenance, quality, discovery and continuous improvement.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices where the wider roadmap justifies it
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, expand or reshape the four-post core and specialist capability only where live-service evidence, broad discovery and the confirmed wider student-journey roadmap justify additional throughput or expertise.

steps.title: Embed an enduring institutional product-development capability
steps.summary: By the end of the three-year mobilisation, establish the sustainable multidisciplinary capability, professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with SED product ownership and Digital and IT specialist/platform services. Decide which elements of the four-post mobilisation core should continue after June 2029 and confirm recurrent staffing, tooling and costs from live evidence before business-as-usual transition.
